author: TheRealMoeder

comments.body:
Hi, fortunately I don't think I need more details. That is a normal failure message that can happen all the time. It just says, that the received websocket packet did not contain a complete JSON document and that there is a parsing error. The packet is then just ignored and the uni-meter continues to process incoming websocket messages. In my environment that happens approximately 3 times each day. 

The only thing that worries me: you are saying the uni-meter stopped working. Are you sure about that? Everything is designed to cope with situtations like that. The worst thing that can happen is that the websocket connection is dropped. But then the Hoymiles storage opens a new connection and everything still works.

Excerpt from my log and everything still works perfect:

```

Would Uni-Meter automatically reopen the sma multicast connection if it somehow stopped receiving data? If not this could be useful.
Yes, everything is designed around the “let it crash” philosophy, a failure can happen and will happen. The SMA multicast socket would be opended again in case of a failure.

I guess I will never reach full compatibility since there are a lot of methods to query and configure the device as well as thinks like webhooks. But I will add enhancements to reach compatibility with certain devices or software tools. So if you need Shelly.GetStatus I will add it :-)

Now I am adding Shelly.GetStatus and then we will see what's needed next instead of taking the specifiction and adding function by function.

If you can send me some information (or point me to the right website) how the Shelly writes its data into mqtt topic, I can also add this.

Great, I will help with testing of course.

Concerning MQTT, I didn't mean Uni-meter should necessarily copy Shelly output but rather offer a config option to add an Mqtt output server and topic to which it could publish energy data.
Let's discuss the MQTT stuff in a new issue, so that I can close this one.

title: Logfile will be overwritten
body: When starting the uni-meter as service the log file /var/log/uni-meter.log starts writing the new log entries at the beginning of the file instead of appending it to the end. That leads to overwriting the previous log entries.
author: StPinkert

comments.body:
You can configure this behavior in the file /opt/uni-meter/config/systemd/uni-meter.service. I will update this in the next release. In the meanwhile you can adjust your configuration file and issue a `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` (replace file: by append:)

[Unit]
Description=Universal power meter converter
After=syslog.target network.target ntp.service

[Service]
ExecStart=/opt/uni-meter/bin/uni-meter.sh
ExecReload=
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/uni-meter.log
StandardError=append:/var/log/uni-meter.log

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

title: not an issue, but would be very helpful for many users - docker compose instructions
body: Is it possible to provide instructions for docker compose?
author: martin-st-81

comments.body: Sure, I will try to provide a docker image together with some instructions ... just give me some time :-)

So, i created a Dockerimage. It will be pushed as

sdeigm/uni-meter:latest

to dockerhub.

I have set up a separate uni-meter-docker github project which contains a docker-compose file.

The project has no readme yet. The docker-compose file will map 3 ports to the container 80/TCP, 1010/UDP and 5353/UDP

The first port if for the Shelly's WebServer, the second one for RCP over UDP and the last one for the avahi mDNS daemon.

If you don't need one of the features, you can just disable the port mapping.

For the avahi daemon you have to decide if you want to use the one from the real host or the one from the docker container. If you want to use the one from the docker container you have to stop the one from the host (if installed at all):
